stem: During an earthquake, which type of waves get generated?
expl: The seismic waves are generated in three forms. (1) P- (Primary) Waves – these waves travel fastest. (2) S - (Secondary) Waves- these waves cause particles to oscillate. Both P and S waves are called ‘Body waves’ because they can travel through the interior of the Earth. (3) Surface Waves – these waves arrive after P and S waves and are confined to the surface of the Earth during an earthquake. There are two types of surface waves (i) Love waves and (ii) Rayleigh waves.

Read the following statement related to 'Earthquake shadow zone' and choose the correct option:
Statement I : The shadow zone of one earthquake is totally different from the shadow zone of another earthquake
Statement II : Seismometers record both 'P' and 'S' waves at any distance out of 105º from earthquake's epicentre

options.label: a
options.text: Statement I and Statement II both are true

options.label: b
options.text: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false

options.label: c
options.text: Statement I is false, but Statement II is true

options.label: d
options.text: Statement I and Statement II both are false

expl: Earthquake waves get recorded in seismographs. However, there exist some specific areas where the waves are not reported. Such a zone is called the 'Shadowzone'. The study of different events reveals that for each earthquake, there exists an altogether different shadow zone. P waves don't arrive between 1050 (1030 - 1050) and 1400 due to refraction at the mantle-core boundary, however S waves don't reappear beyond an angular distance of ~ 1300 as they are stopped by the liquid outer core.

stem:
Consider the following statements :
1. The Richter scale is a logarithmic scale and so an increase of 1 magnitude unit represents a factor of 10 in amplitude.
2. Each integer reading of the Richter scale has an energy 100 times that the previous integer reading.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
expl: The magnitude of the earthquake is measured on the Richter scale and intensity on the Mercalli scale. In 1935, seismologist Charles Francis Richter of the California Institute of Technology developed the Richter magnitude scale. It is based on a logarithmic scale whose base is 10. Each number on the seismogram represents 10 times amplitude and 32 times energy release. A seismic wave of magnitude 1 releases the energy of 6 ounces of TNT. Hence statement (1) is correct while statement (2) is wrong.

stem:
Consider the following statement about earthquake –
1. Intensity of earthquake is measured on Mercalli Scale.
2. Earthquake’s magnitude is the measurement of energy released.
3. Magnitude of earthquake depends directly upon Amplitude of an earthquake waves.
4. Every integer on Richter Scale shows a 100 times increase in energy released
Which of the statements are true?
expl: The intensity of an earthquake is measured by the Mercalli scale. Hence, statement (1) is correct. The magnitude of an earthquake is the measurement of energy released, thus statement (2) is correct. The Richter scale has a shaking amplitude 10 times that of the previous integer and shows an increase of 32 times in energy release. Energy equal to 6 ounces of TNT is released by an earthquake of a magnitude of 1. Hence statement (3) is correct but statement (4) is false.

stem: Which of the following instruments is used to record seismic waves?
expl: A seismograph is an instrument used to detect and record earthquakes. The seismometer is the internal part of the seismograph, which may be a pendulum or a weight mounted on a spring. However, it is also commonly used as a synonym for seismograph. A seismogram is a recording of an earthquake at a specific location on a seismograph instrument. Hence seismograph usually refers to the seismometer and its recording device as a single unit.

stem: Tsunami word belongs to which of the following languages ?
expl: Tsunami is a Japanese word "tsu" which means 'harbor' and "nami" means 'wave'. Thus tsunami means 'harbor wave' arising as a result of the earthquake. These ruptured high waves may cause substantial damage to coastal areas.

stem: Which one of the following statements about the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and the resulting Tsunami is not correct?

options.label: a
options.text: The earthquake originated due to slipping of about 1,200 km of fault line by 15 m along the subduction zone where the India Plate subducts the Burma plate at the Sunda Trench.

options.label: b
options.text: The resulting tsunami devastated the shores ranging from the coast of Indonesia to the east coast of Africa, some 8,500 km away from the epicenter.

options.label: c
options.text: As per the current estimates, the quake-generated tsunami killed more than 50 lakh people, in addition to unaccounted dead bodies swept out to sea.

options.label: d
options.text: Bangladesh had very few casualties because the quake-affected fault line was in a nearly north-south orientation, the greatest strength of the tsunami waves was in an east-west direction.

expl: Undersea earthquake in the Indian Ocean on 26 December, 2004 produced a tsunami that caused huge natural disaster and over 2 lakh people lost their lives. The earthquake took place in the Indian Ocean off the western coast of Sumatra Island of Indonesia. In regards to the options the details of the tsunami are as follows : Statement (a) – An estimated 1300 Km. of fault line slipped about 15 metres. The earthquake occurred on the interface of the India and Burma tectonic plates. Thus statement (a) is almost right. Statement (b) – The waves devasteted the shores of Indonesia, Sri Lanka and India as far as Somalia on the east coast of Africa. Hence this statement is also nearly true. Statement (c) – Approximately 2-3 Lakhs people were estimated to have lost their lives. Thus statement (c) is wrong. Statement (d) – Bangladesh, which lies at the northern end of the Bay of Bengal had very few casualties. So, statement (d) is true.

stem: Which city of Japan had faced tsunami and nuclear radiation recently ?
expl: A major earthquake on 11th March, 2011 with a magnitude (Mw) of 9.0 in Fukushima caused large damage in Japan. Due to this disaster, nuclear power plants were damaged which finally resulted in nuclear radiation.

stem: The North-Western Region of the Indian Sub-continent is susceptible to earthquake activity because of –
expl: North-Western region of the Indian Subcontinent is susceptible to earthquake activities because it is situated at the border of plates. This area is convergence region of the Indian Plate and the Eurasian Plate. Coral formation activities and volcanic activities do not occur here.

stem: The place on earth's surface which records the seismic wave first, is called :
expl: The point where the energy is released is called the focus of an earthquake. The point/place where the seismic waves are first recorded is called the epicentre.
